description: Soft, fluffy, and so easy to make! These are my grandma’s famous sugar cookies and these little tips make them turn out perfect every time! Think soft, almost cake like cookies with the prettiest royal icing. Perfect for Easter! And if you love a pretty kitchen moment as much as I do, all the utensils I used are @MacKenzie-Childs Rosy Check! #mcpartner  ICING RECIPE: Beat: 3 TBSP Meringue Powder 1/2 + cup Warm Water (Until frothy) Add: 4 Cups Powdered Sugar (Slowly until glossy) Add: Vanilla to taste and more water if the icing is too stiff. This dries pretty fast (within 5-10 minutes) GRANDMA’S SOFT SUGAR COOKIE RECIPE: 1 Cup Soft Butter 11/2 Cups Sugar 2 Eggs 1 Cup Sour Cream 11/2 TSP Vanilla 41/2 Cups Flour 1 TSP Salt 1 TSP Baking Soda 1/2 TSP Nutmeg Cream butter and sugar till fluffy, add eggs and beat well. Add sour cream and vanilla, blend well. Add dry ingredients. The dough will get quite soft. Chill for several hours or over night is best. Roll to 1/4 inch thickness, cut, (sprinkle with sugar if you don’t plan to frost), and bake at 375 for 8-12 minutes just until some edges get barely golden). Undercooked is better than overcooked.  #eastercookies #royalicing #pinkkitchen #sugarcookies
transcript: You will officially retire every single sugar cookie recipe after you try these. These are my grandma's super soft fluffy sour cream sugar cookies, and what's crazy is they get softer and softer each day. They are very simple to make, but these tips will help you make them perfect every time. First, refrigerate your dough for at least an hour. Next, you want to flour everything, and I mean everything. The dough softens very quickly and can get sticky, so this makes cutting out your shapes much easier. For icing, I always like to use meringue powder and a little trick. Place your piping bags and cups to fill them, and then once the hole is cut, flip the tops upward so nothing leaks out. The icing is intentionally very thin, but that's what gives you this beautiful watercolor effect. I'll list the full recipe in the caption. These are perfect for Easter.
